angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 2,392,512 km at 27.40 pc = 1.17 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 23875: distance 27.397 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.012), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 27.397 +/- 0.329 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 36.2456 +/- 0.3575 mas (same row, RUWE 2.68), 101.4 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 3.439 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 23875: radius 3.439 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 43.469 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.035) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 2,392,512 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 7997 +/- 144 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 23875: effective temperature 7997 +/- 144 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.028) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 23875: effective temperature 7997 +/- 144 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.028) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Pulkovo spectrophotometric catalogue, table 5 (320-1080 nm, 2.5 nm steps, 10 nm resolution, absolute flux in W m^-2 m^-1)) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
